security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU ACLIC MMIO write handler permits modification of read-only IE and IP fields in sourcecfgK registers, allowing guest software to fabricate interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable state that should only be controlled through setipnum/clripnum/setienum/clrienum
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: sourcecfgK IE/IP fields writable despite RO spec | ACLIC mmio_write sourcecfg no RO mask
security_spec.summary: ACLIC redesigned from indirect-CSR to APLIC-subset MMIO: sourcecfgK embeds read-only IE/IP mirrors replacing pending/enable arrays; QEMU must enforce RO semantics or guest can forge interrupt state

findings.finding: sourcecfg MMIO write handler correctly masks write values. For non-delegated sources, only D (bit 10) and SM (bits 2:0) are writable via mask 'APLIC_SOURCECFG_D | APLIC_SOURCECFG_SM_MASK'. For delegated sources, only D and CHILDIDX (bits 9:0) are writable. IE and IP bits are NOT stored in sourcecfg registers at all — they reside in the separate state[] array controlled exclusively through SETIPNUM/CLRIPNUM/SETIENUM/CLRIENUM registers. No path exists for guest software to fabricate interrupt-enable or interrupt-pending state via sourcecfg writes.

Side-effects after sourcecfg write are correct: when source becomes delegated or inactive (SM=INACTIVE), both pending (IP) and enabled (IE) bits are forcibly cleared via riscv_aplic_set_pending_raw/enabled_raw. When source becomes active with rectified input=1, pending is set. This prevents stale IE/IP state from persisting across source configuration changes.

SETIPNUM/CLRIPNUM handler (via riscv_aplic_set_pending) correctly gates pending modifications through riscv_aplic_source_active() check. Inactive or delegated sources silently ignore set-pending writes. For level-triggered sources in MSI mode, additional rectified-input consistency checks prevent spurious pending state. This ensures IP state can only be modified for active, non-delegated sources in valid trigger modes.

SETIENUM/CLRIENUM handler (via riscv_aplic_set_enabled) correctly gates enable modifications through riscv_aplic_source_active() check. Inactive or delegated sources silently ignore set-enable writes. This ensures IE state can only be modified for active, non-delegated sources.

sourcecfg read path correctly returns the raw sourcecfg register value. IE/IP bits are not in sourcecfg, so reads of sourcecfg cannot leak IE/IP state. The separate SETIP/CLRIP/SETIE/CLRIE base-register read paths (lines 664-686) explicitly return pending/enabled word values via dedicated read functions, not via sourcecfg registers.

Migration state (vmstate_riscv_aplic) includes both sourcecfg[] and state[] arrays as separate VMSTATE_VARRAY_UINT32 fields with num_irqs sizing. IE and IP bits are embedded in state[] alongside the INPUT bit. This is architecturally correct — there are no missing fields that would cause silent corruption on live-migration. The domaincfg, MSI config addresses, idelivery, iforce, and ithreshold arrays are also all present.
findings.snippet:
VMSTATE_VARRAY_UINT32(sourcecfg, RISCVAPLICState,
                              num_irqs, 0,
                              vmstate_info_uint32, uint32_t),
        VMSTATE_VARRAY_UINT32(state, RISCVAPLICState,
                              num_irqs, 0,
                              vmstate_info_uint32, uint32_t),

findings.finding: Reset/realize initializes sourcecfg, state, and target arrays via g_new0 (zero-initialized). All sources start in SM=INACTIVE (0) with no pending/enabled bits set. This is correct per spec — no interrupts are active or pending at reset. Default target in non-MSI mode is set to 1 (hart index 0, iprio=1). No IE/IP corruption possible at initialization.

Hardware interrupt request path (@riscv_aplic_request) correctly delegates to child APLICs for delegated sources. For local sources, it checks edge/level trigger modes and only sets pending raw (IPCORE path through riscv_aplic_set_pending_raw). It does NOT set IE bits. The INPUT state bit is updated separately from IP. This clean separation prevents the HW IRQ path from fabricating interrupt-enable state.

State structure cleanly separates sourcecfg (configuration: D, SM, CHILDIDX) from state[] (runtime: IP, IE, INPUT bit flags). The IE/IP fields exist only in state[], which is mutated exclusively through setipnum/clripnum/setienum/clrienum accessors. No field aliasing or union tricks could allow sourcecfg writes to corrupt IE/IP. The struct layout matches the architectural register separation.

SETIP/CLRIP/SETIE/CLRIE bitfield-word write handlers (SETIP_BASE, CLRIP_BASE, SETIE_BASE, CLRIE_BASE) and their num-register variants (SETIPNUM, CLRIPNUM, SETIENUM, CLRIENUM) all route through riscv_aplic_set_pending/set_enabled which gate on source_active(). No direct write path from MMIO to the state[] IP/IE bits bypasses the active-source guard. Write values to bitfield registers are properly used as bit-masks to select which IRQs to affect.
